item.title: Integrated DInSAR and HVSR microtremor analysis for understanding ground deformation and site effects: case study of the Bawean earthquake (M6.5)
item.description: This study investigates the seismic hazards of Bawean Island following a recent M6.5 earthquake using an integrated approach combining differential interferometric synthetic aperture radar (DInSAR) and horizontal-to-vertical spectral ratio (HVSR) methodologies. item.title: Effects of seismic filters on pretrained CNN models for fault detection: application to the Delft 3D seismic volume, the Netherlands
item.description: Accurate mapping of faults from 3D seismic volumes is critical for identifying structural traps, assessing reservoir compartmentalization, and guiding drilling decisions. This study evaluates how common seismic conditioning filters affect both the visual quality of a production Delft 3D poststack time-migrated volume and the outputs of two pretrained 3D CNN fault detectors: UNet3D and FaultNet. item.title: Numerical study of porosity effects on temperature and fluid flow in Black Sea gas hydrates
item.description: Numerical temperature and fluid flow simulations were conducted using ANSYS Fluent to investigate the influence of porosity variations on the temperature distribution within the gas hydrate layer. The study was carried out in the Black Sea region, where the gas hydrate deposits are of particular interest due to their potential for energy resources. item.title: Latest sightings of the striped hyena in North Africa: major threats and conservation actions
item.description: The striped hyena (Hyaena hyaena) is widely distributed across the northern half of Africa, the Middle East, the Arabian Peninsula, and parts of Asia. However, numerous studies indicate that this carnivore is in decline, and it is currently classified as near threatened on the IUCN Red List of threatened species. In North Africa, the Hyaena hyaena barbara subspecies has been extirpated from many areas. This article summarizes data collected from observations of the striped hyena in North Africa

item.title: Stage-specific growth characteristics of the calanoid copepod invader Sinodiaptomus sarsi​
item.description: The population dynamics of the Asian invasive copepod Sinodiaptomus sarsi were studied for four years after its introduction into an artificial pond in Kyiv (Ukraine) in 2020. The growth and development parameters of this species were measured under laboratory conditions. item.title: Nonnative crayfish in Türkiye: presence records, invasion pathways, and ecological risks
item.description: The globalization of trade, aquaculture, and the ornamental pet industry has accelerated the transboundary movement of nonnative crayfish species, with significant ecological consequences. Türkiye, a biodiversity-rich country bridging Europe and Asia, has increasingly become a point of concern due to the rising presence of alien crayfish taxa introduced primarily via the aquarium trade and scientific research. item.title: Morphometric and reproductive divergence of deep-water shrimps Plesionika martia (A. Milne-Edwards, 1883) and P. heterocarpus (A. Costa, 1871) along a depth gradient in the eastern Aegean Sea
item.description: This study provides a comparative analysis of two deep-water pandalid shrimp species, Plesionika martia and P. heterocarpus, based on monthly samples collected over one year in the Eastern Aegean Sea. item.title: Frequencies and roles of plants in the diet of three mesocarnivores (Canis lupaster, Genetta genetta, and Herpestes ichneumon): implications for forest regeneration in a North African hot spot (Algeria)
item.description: The Djurdjura National Park (PND, Algeria) is part of one of the world’s 36 biodiversity hot spots, recognised by the United Nations as a national biosphere reserve. It contains the Darna primary forest, a key habitat for several mesocarnivore mammals, including the golden wolf (Canis lupaster), the common genet (Genetta genetta) and the ichneumon mongoose (Herpestes ichneumon). item.title: Species identification using otolith morphometry of four gurnards (Family: Triglidae) from Edremit Bay (Aegean Sea)
item.description: Shape and size analyses of otoliths are widely considered appropriate tools for distinguishing between fish species and for assessing populations and stocks. The present study aims to distinguish four gurnard species collected from Edremit Bay (Aegean Sea) based on variations in their otolith shape morphology.
